sentences.text:
The present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the petitioner assailing the order dated 06.02.2014 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Guna in Criminal Revision No.160/2013, whereby the revision preferred by respondent No.1 was allowed and the order dated 29.08.2013 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Raghogarh in Case No.670/2013 taking cognizance against the respondent No.1 under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code was set aside.
2.

Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that the petitioner filed a private complaint before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raghogarh alleging that the accused persons, in collusion, obtained unlawful benefit for each other.

It was specifically alleged that respondent No.1/K.K. Srivastava,
while functioning as Sub-Registrar, Raghogarh, despite written intimation from the petitioner not to register the disputed sale deed, went ahead and registered the same in favour of the co-accused persons, thereby causing loss NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20844 2 MCRC-3588-2014 to the petitioner.

3. Upon considering the statements of the complainant and her witnesses under Sections 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C. and perusing the documents on record, the learned Magistrate by order dated 29.08.2013 took cognizance against accused Ram Prasad, Ram Singh, Smt. Nandu Saini, Rajkishore Saini, and respondent No.1/K.K. Srivastava under Section 420 of IPC and directed registration of a criminal case.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved, respondent No.1 preferred Criminal Revision No.160/2013, which came to be allowed by the revisional court vide order dated 06.02.2014.

The revisional court held that no offence under Section 420 IPC was made out against respondent No.1 as he had acted in discharge of his official duties as Sub-Registrar, and therefore set aside the order of cognizance.
5. The present petition has been filed on the ground that the revisional court erred in interfering with the order of the Magistrate.

It was averred therein that (i) the impugned order is contrary to law, (ii) the revisional court had no jurisdiction to pass the order under Section 203 Cr.P.C., (iii) in view of Section 397(2) Cr.P.C., the revision petition was not maintainable, and (iv) sufficient evidence existed against the respondent No.1 to justify cognizance.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, this Court finds no merit in the petition.
The revisional court has rightly observed that the act of registration of a sale deed by respondent No.1 was in discharge of his official duties as Sub-Registrar.

The allegations made NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20844 3 MCRC-3588-2014 in the complaint,
even if accepted in entirety, do not disclose dishonest or fraudulent intention on part of respondent No.1 at the inception of the transaction so as to constitute the offence of cheating under Section 420 IPC.
7.

The ground raised by the petitioner that the revision petition was barred under Section 397(2)
Cr.P.C. is misconceived.
The impugned order of the Magistrate taking cognizance and directing registration of a case is not an interlocutory order and was, therefore, amenable to revisional jurisdiction.
8. The further ground raised herein that the revisional court exercised powers under Section 203 Cr.P.C. is also devoid of substance.

The revisional court has not passed an order under Section 203 but has exercised jurisdiction under Section 397 Cr.P.C. to test the correctness, legality, and propriety of the order passed by the Magistrate.
9. It is well-settled that the extraordinary powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. are to be exercised sparingly and with circumspection.
Interference is warranted only where there is manifest illegality or miscarriage of justice.
In the present case, the order of the revisional court does not suffer from any illegality, perversity, or irregularity warranting interference.
10. Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the present petition is devoid of merit.
The petition stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE ojha Smt.Neetu Jain vs K.K.Shrivastava on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170515252/
